intro: Picture this: you wake up in a room set in a fruit orchard, open the door to cool air and birdsong in a mangosteen grove, then walk just a few minutes to a waterfall — Baansuanrudee Resort (Baan Suan Rudee Resort) is a small resort of about 10 rooms tucked into Trok Nong sub-district, Khlung district, Chanthaburi, only about 400 metres from Trok Nong Waterfall · what guests remember is the quiet of being in nature, the country-garden feel, and an outdoor pool to soak in after a day of hiking and waterfall walks · rooms start at about THB 1,500/night with air conditioning, a fridge, satellite TV and Wi-Fi, plus a restaurant and a grill area · it is a small place that leans on garden atmosphere and nature rather than luxury, a good fit for couples and families who drive themselves and want to escape the city for a quiet garden stay.

body.html: The big picture and who it suits — to put it the way a friend would, Baansuanrudee Resort, or Baan Suan Rudee Resort in Thai, is not a big hotel in town but a small resort of about 10 rooms built in the middle of a fruit orchard in Trok Nong sub-district, Khlung district, Chanthaburi · its charm really lives in the words "country garden" — this is not a place selling a fancy lobby or a sea view, but the feeling of "arrive, drop your bags, fill your lungs with orchard air, and sit listening to a waterfall not far off in the evening" · Trok Nong is an area known for its lush forest and fruit orchards, especially good-quality mangosteen and durian, which gives this place a cool, shaded atmosphere from the trees around it that you simply cannot get in a city hotel · from the property details and what is said about it across several travel sites, the people who say they love it tend to be couples who want a quiet trip into nature and families or groups of friends who drive in from Bangkok to visit the waterfall and orchards · another group it suits especially well is people coming during fruit season (April to June) who want to base themselves near the orchards to taste durian and mangosteen fresh off the tree · on the flip side, if you are after a five-star resort where every detail is polished, with a spa, gym, a lavish breakfast buffet and chain-hotel service, this may not be the answer, because its whole identity is a small place in a garden built around nature and a friendly price · put simply, if you come for "nature, the waterfall and quiet," it does that well at an easy price, but if you come for "luxury and every amenity covered," you should look at hotels in central Chanthaburi instead.

Location and getting there — Trok Nong sub-district sits in Khlung district, east of Chanthaburi town, a foothill area full of fruit orchards and waterfalls · Baan Suan Rudee's address is 45/6 Moo 2, Trok Nong sub-district, Khlung district, Chanthaburi 22110 · the standout feature of this location is that it is only about 400 metres from Trok Nong Waterfall, close enough that you can almost walk there · Trok Nong is a three-tier waterfall in green forest that many rate as quieter and less crowded than Phlio Waterfall, with the top tier about 20 metres high, lovely in the rainy season through early winter when the water is high · from Bangkok it is about 4 to 4.5 hours of driving via the motorway and the eastern highway, then you branch off toward Phlio Waterfall heading for Trat, reach the junction into Khlung district, turn onto the Khlung–Makham road for about another 10 kilometres to Trok Nong market, then turn onto the waterfall road · nearby spots you can easily add on are Phlio Waterfall, Chanthaburi's popular national park about 20–30 min drive away, and the Chanthaboon Waterfront Community, a photogenic old quarter about 30–40 min drive away · the honest caveat is that the resort is in a garden in the countryside, a fair way from Chanthaburi town with almost no public transport around here, so without your own car it is very awkward · if you fly in, you land at Trat Airport (TDX), about 46 kilometres away, or U-Tapao Airport (UTP), then pick up a rental car, but driving yourself is still the most convenient way for a place like this.

"What I love is how genuinely quiet it is — you wake up to nothing but birds and cool air from the garden, walk to Trok Nong Waterfall in a few minutes, and come back in the evening to soak in the cool pool · coming during fruit season is even better, you get to eat fresh mangosteen and durian right there. It suits anyone who wants to escape the city and rest in nature, nice and quiet."

Room types and decor — Baan Suan Rudee is a small resort of about 10 rooms, so it feels private and never crowded · from the property details, the rooms split into three main types: Standard mountain view (one large single bed plus a sofa bed, good for couples or a small family), Family waterfall view (two double beds, good for a family or group of friends) and Superior waterfall view (two single beds) · every room has the basics covered — air conditioning, a fridge, satellite TV, a private bathroom and free drinking water — and some have a balcony or terrace to sit out and catch the garden breeze · the decor is a simple garden-resort style that leans on cleanliness and comfort over luxury, blending in with the trees around it · something many people like is the room names "waterfall view" and "mountain view," which point to the genuine natural surroundings — even if not every room sees the waterfall itself clearly, you still get the garden and green hills as a backdrop · because this is a small, owner-run place, the finish of the decor is straightforward, without the bold design flourishes of a boutique hotel, which fits the character of a garden resort built for real use · the tip here is that since each room type differs in size, bed count and view, if you care about the view or the number of guests, you should ask for details and request photos of the exact room you will get when you book directly, because for a small place like this the room information on online booking platforms is sometimes not complete for every type.

Facilities, the pool and nature activities — the heart of Baan Suan Rudee is the garden atmosphere and nature around it, but what sets it apart from the usual small place is that it has an outdoor pool for guests to soak and cool off in, which is rare in a small place at this price · the pool sits amid green garden, perfect for a soak after a day out at the waterfall or the orchards · besides the pool there is a shaded garden to wander, a BBQ/grill area, an on-site restaurant, free parking and free Wi-Fi · the real highlight of staying here is walking out to Trok Nong Waterfall, only about 400 metres away, a three-tier waterfall in the forest where you can swim in the lower tiers when the water is high, with a camping ground for those who want the full nature experience · during Chanthaburi's fruit season (roughly April to June), the Trok Nong area also has orchards open for tasting fresh mangosteen and durian off the tree, an activity that fits a garden stay like this · to be honest, there is no spa, gym or big-resort facilities here, and the pool is a modest size for soaking rather than serious swimming laps · but for anyone who already sees the waterfall and orchards as their own natural playground, what this place has is enough for a simple garden getaway.

Food and dining — Baan Suan Rudee has an on-site restaurant serving made-to-order dishes and drinks, so guests do not have to drive far when hunger hits, which matters a lot for a garden place far from town restaurants · from the property details, several sources say breakfast is available, but others say otherwise, so you should ask at booking whether breakfast is included and whether it is a set or a choice of menu, because a small place may adjust by the number of guests at times · something many guests love is the BBQ/grill area, where you can buy fresh ingredients and cook your own in the garden in the evening — a popular activity for groups who drive themselves and want a small party vibe with friends or family in nature · beyond that, Khlung district itself and Trok Nong market have local restaurants and food to try within an easy drive, and if you head toward Chanthaburi town you will find the city's well-known eateries such as Chanthaburi rice noodles (sen chan) and seafood · overall, food is not the reason to come and eat at the property as your main plan, but having a restaurant and a grill area on site means dining is not a problem for people staying in a garden like this.

Service — because Baan Suan Rudee is a small resort looked after closely by the owner or staff, its charm in service is a country-garden friendliness rather than chain-hotel professionalism · what is said about it on travel sites reflects that the staff are friendly, helpful and happy to recommend routes to the waterfall, orchards and nearby spots · check-in is around 2 PM to 9 PM and check-out in the morning to about 11 AM, so if you will arrive late you should let them know in advance · one thing to understand is that for a small place like this, some contact and booking happens by phone or Facebook directly alongside online booking platforms, and replies may sometimes not be as fast as a big hotel · some sources also state that pets are not accepted here, so if you plan to bring a dog or cat you should confirm with the property every time and not assume · overall, the service at a small garden place like this is a warm friendliness traded for a flexibility that may not be as exacting as a big hotel, which most people who choose to stay here understand and accept.

Voices from real reviews — both praise and gripes — to be honest, Baan Suan Rudee is a small place that has a number of reviews on online booking platforms but not a great many, with an average score around 7.9 from a few dozen real guests on Agoda, while some platforms like Tripadvisor give a lower average of around 6.0 across cleanliness, facilities, location and service · the differing numbers reflect that the experience depends quite a bit on expectations and when you go, so they are better read as part of your decision than as a fixed score · on the praise side: what comes up most is the location within walking distance of Trok Nong Waterfall, the quiet, shaded atmosphere amid the fruit orchard, having a pool to soak in at a budget place, and the value compared with other places in the same area · on the watch-out side: what to understand before booking is that this is a small place where the facilities and room details are basic and straightforward, some reviews feel cleanliness and upkeep in places are only middling, the property is far from town so you need your own car, and breakfast/service can at times be inconsistent in keeping with a small place's character · these notes are mostly about setting your expectations right — that this is a small garden resort built around nature and price, not a full-service resort.

"It's a small place but the garden atmosphere is really good, quiet and shaded, and having a pool to swim in makes it worth the price · the only downside is that some corners of the upkeep are still a bit homespun and it's far from town so you have to drive yourself, but if you're here for Trok Nong Waterfall and the orchards, this location is the most convenient there is."

Price and value — to be honest, this is not a luxury resort, and it never meant to be · the real selling point of Baan Suan Rudee is sleeping in a fruit orchard near a waterfall, with a pool to soak in, at a price you can reach · rooms start at about THB 1,500/night in the regular range and rise with the room type and the time of year, especially fruit season and long weekends when people flock to Chanthaburi · compared with hotels in central Chanthaburi like KP Grand or Maneechan Resort, which have more complete facilities but are not right by nature, Baan Suan Rudee plays a different game — it is the choice for a small, budget place for people who want to wake up in a garden and walk to a waterfall rather than a hotel in town · its value lies in having a pool for a little over a thousand baht, plus a location by the waterfall you cannot get in a city hotel · if you are planning to visit Trok Nong Waterfall, Phlio Waterfall and the orchards on the Khlung side, staying here saves both time and travel costs, and the few thousand baht you spend is worth it for the atmosphere you get · but if you expect polished hotel-grade rooms and full service, you should raise your budget and stay in town instead.

What to know before booking — there are several things that make the stay smoother · one, you should have your own car, because the property is in a garden in Trok Nong sub-district, far from Chanthaburi town with almost no public transport around here, so without driving yourself getting around is hard · two, ask about the room details and the exact view you will get when you book, because there are several room types with mountain views and waterfall views differing in size and bed count, and if you care about the view or the number of guests you should specify from the start · three, ask clearly about breakfast and pets, because the information from various sources does not match — some say breakfast is available, some say it is not, and some state pets are not accepted, so confirm with the property directly first · four, check when the waterfall is at its best — Trok Nong has the most water and is prettiest from the rainy season through early winter (roughly July to December), while in the dry season the water may be low, so if you come mainly for the waterfall, plan your timing well · five, come during fruit season for a bonus — roughly April to June is durian and mangosteen season in Trok Nong, and staying here makes it easy to go out and taste fresh fruit from the orchards, but the place fills up fast then, so book ahead · six, during long weekends and high season a small place like this fills up fast, so book and confirm well in advance.

The verdict — from all the property details and everything said about it, Baansuanrudee Resort (Baan Suan Rudee Resort) is a small place in a Trok Nong fruit orchard that suits people who value nature, the waterfall and quiet over luxury · a location within a few minutes' walk of Trok Nong Waterfall, a quiet, shaded setting amid mangosteen and durian groves, plus a pool to soak in starting at a little over a thousand baht, make it a lovely choice for couples and families who drive themselves and want to escape the city to be with nature on the Khlung side · if you are looking for a hotel with polished rooms, a spa, a gym and full service like a big hotel, this is not the answer, and you should consider a hotel in central Chanthaburi instead · but for a simple nature trip where you want to wake up in a garden, walk to play in a waterfall, soak in the pool to beat the heat and taste fresh fruit from the orchards — Baan Suan Rudee does that in a way a city hotel cannot, and that is why its name keeps coming up on the list of Trok Nong stays that waterfall travellers recommend.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Baansuanrudee Resort (Baan Suan Rudee Resort)

faq.q: Where is Baan Suan Rudee Resort, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It sits in a fruit orchard at 45/6 Moo 2, Trok Nong, Khlung district, Chanthaburi, only about 400 metres from Trok Nong Waterfall · from Bangkok it is about 4–4.5 hours of driving, with free parking · it is about 30–40 min drive from Chanthaburi town, and there is almost no public transport around here, so you should have your own car.

faq.q: What is the starting price at Baan Suan Rudee, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start at about THB 1,500/night for the Standard mountain-view room · there is also a Superior waterfall view and a Family waterfall view for families, with prices varying by room type and season · it fills up fast in fruit season and on long weekends, so book and confirm in advance.

faq.q: Does Baan Suan Rudee have a pool?
faq.a: Yes · it is an outdoor pool amid the garden, for soaking and cooling off after a day out at the waterfall and orchards · it counts as a standout that is hard to find in a small place for a little over a thousand baht · it is a pool for soaking rather than serious swimming laps.

faq.q: How close is Baan Suan Rudee to Trok Nong Waterfall, and when is the waterfall at its best?
faq.a: The property is only about 400 metres from Trok Nong Waterfall, within walking distance · Trok Nong is a three-tier waterfall in the forest, with the top tier about 20 metres high · it has the most water and is prettiest from the rainy season through early winter (roughly Jul–Dec); in the dry season the water may be low, so if you come for the waterfall, choose your timing well.

faq.q: Can you bring pets to Baan Suan Rudee, and is breakfast available?
faq.a: The information from various sources does not match — on pets, some sources say they are not accepted, and on breakfast, some say it is available and some say it is not · so you should contact the property to confirm directly before booking every time, and not assume.

faq.q: Who is Baan Suan Rudee good for?
faq.a: It suits couples and families/groups of friends who drive themselves and want a quiet nature trip in a garden, and people visiting Trok Nong Waterfall, Phlio Waterfall and the orchards on the Khlung side · it has a pool and a grill area on site · if you are looking for a hotel with polished rooms, a spa and full service like a big hotel, this may not match what you want, and you should look at hotels in town instead.
